about: Part of the reference catalogue: designed experiments from one published source, for testing that software reproduces them.
McMullen and Jurica (2024) optimise a methoxylation by SNOBFIT, each reaction followed as a time course of the product's
LC area percent, and model the 15 reactions nearest the optimum by functional principal component analysis and a
stepwise quadratic regression of the FPC scores. Only the electronic supplementary information is captured. Each
expected item has its printed text, where it is printed (a page of the ESI and a quotation) and a check, or manual:
the reason it is not recomputed. not_captured lists what was left out. Read with

source.title: Accelerating reaction optimization through data-rich experimentation and machine-assisted process development
source.cite: McMullen and Jurica (2024), "Accelerating reaction optimization through data-rich experimentation and machine-assisted process development", Reaction Chemistry & Engineering 9(8), 2160-2170, electronic supplementary information
source.read: 2026-10-31, the electronic supplementary information (37 pages); the article itself was not read
source.rights: The article and its electronic supplementary information are protected by copyright (The Royal Society of Chemistry 2024) and are not reproduced here; read them through the DOI. This file holds facts they report (numbers and experimental data) and short quotations that locate each one, for citation and for checking software. The MIT licence of process-improve does not extend to them.

experiments.name: mcmullen-jurica-methoxylation-fpca
experiments.title: Methoxylation optimised by SNOBFIT in four rounds of ten reactions, each a time course of the product's LC area percent; FPCA of the 15 reactions nearest the optimum and a stepwise quadratic model of their FPC scores

factors.name: Temperature
factors.description: reaction temperature; the upper bound was raised from 80 to 85 degC after round 1, so coded values reach 1.25

responses.name: fpc_score
responses.description: the reaction's score on the one functional principal component of its LCAP time course (Table S9); printed for the 15 reactions nearest experiment 34 only

responses.name: lcap
responses.description: LC area percent of product 2 over the reaction (Table S7, column '2 LCAP'); 9 to 12 samples per reaction

argument.name: time
argument.units: coded as printed: 0 to 1, and 1.25 when the reaction ran 30 h, so hours / 24

design.details: Four rounds of ten reactions chosen by the SNOBFIT algorithm (Table S4: Npoint 10, Nreq 10), some added by the scientist (grey rows of Table S7). Experiment = 10 * (round - 1) + reaction. The 15 reactions modelled in Tables S9 and S10 are those nearest experiment 34 by Mahalanobis distance.

runs.notes: One row per reaction, from Table S7: its settings, its FPC score from Table S9 (null when not printed), and its samples in order, time_j with lcap_j, null-padded to 12. CuBr is printed as 0.556, 0.667 and 0.778 for 6, 7 and 8 mol%: exactly 5/9, 6/9 and 7/9 in coded units, and the regression of Table S10 reproduces only with those exact values. The column 'Obj. Fun.' of Table S7 is not captured.

experiments.notes: Three things in the source disagree with each other, each checked here. (1) Table S7 prints round 2's reactions 7 to 10 twice, row for row; they are kept once. (2) Table S9 prints DMF as 0.96 for experiment 12 and 0.88 for experiment 25; Table S7 prints the reverse (0.88 and 0.96). Table S10 reproduces with Table S7's values and not with Table S9's (the intercept comes out -1107 instead of -582.5), so the runs here carry Table S7's. (3) Figure S7's parity plot spans -20 to 20, while Table S9's scores span -97.28 to 104.76: the plotted scores are not the tabulated ones.

not_captured: The bromination case study (Tables S5, S6, S8 and S11, Eq. S13, Figures S2 and S8): a quadratic model of the assay yield at 8 h, fitted in real units to runs printed in coded units.
Tables S1 and S2: the UPLC methods. Tables S4 and S6: the SNOBFIT settings, inputs to an algorithm the library does not have.
Table S7, column 'Obj. Fun.': the objective SNOBFIT maximised, derived from LCAP.
Figures S1, S4 and S5: plots of the time courses captured as runs; Figure S3: the sorted Mahalanobis distances, not printed as numbers.
